DECISION-REGISTER ENTRY
DR-ID: 2026-06-26T21-32-33Z-home-defer-inc2.1
WHEN: 2026-06-26T21:32:33Z
CHECKPOINT: directive-lock
DILEMMA: where the builder-deploy-core skill permanently lives — Option A the-stoa forge-owned home vs Option B a standalone builder-tooling location — trades discoverability plus riding the-stoa install/arc lifecycle (A) against decoupled release cadence plus conceptual fit as a standalone product (B).
WARNING: building increment 2.1 before the permanent HOME is chosen accepts that a wrong neutral-location bet could force rework at 2.3; mitigated because the package layout is HOME-independent by construction so relocation is intended to be an additive git mv, but that mitigation is unproven until the actual 2.3 relocation happens.
OPTIONS: A the-stoa forge-owned home (couples builder tooling to the substrate-deploy lifecycle) ~ B standalone builder-tooling location (stands up a home for a consumer that does not yet exist) ~ DEFER the permanent choice to 2.3 and build 2.1 in a decision-neutral the-stoa/agents location now (accepts deciding later, B leading future candidate)
CHOSEN: DEFER the permanent choice to 2.3 and build 2.1 in a decision-neutral the-stoa/agents location now (B leading future candidate)
COUNTER-HYPOTHESIS: if at increment 2.3 the chosen permanent HOME requires more than an additive git mv plus an install/consume-path update — i.e. the relocation forces a redesign of the builder_deploy_core package layout or its data/ plus tests/ structure — then the HOME-independent-layout premise was false and building-neutral-now was the wrong call.
CONTEXT-LINK: stoa--pj3 (u--9s2 Phase-2 increment 2.1); ratified by Polybius_the_Stoa 2026-06-26T21:32:33Z; design-rev2 section 4

DECISION-REGISTER ENTRY
DR-ID: 2026-06-27T04-34-57Z-home-A-ratified-inc2.3
WHEN: 2026-06-27T04:34:57Z
CHECKPOINT: directive-lock
DILEMMA: where the builder-deploy skill permanently lives, trading discoverability plus riding the-stoa arc/install.sh/gauntlet lifecycle (forge-owned) against decoupled release cadence plus conceptual fit as a standalone product serving builders outside the-stoa orbit (standalone).
WARNING: choosing A accepts that builder-deploy ultimately serves builders outside the-stoa orbit, so until graduation a non-the-stoa consumer (e.g. scienceclaw at 2.4) must install the whole the-stoa substrate to obtain the skill; A also bets the A-to-B graduation stays an additive git mv (the HOME-independent-layout premise), unproven until the actual relocation.
OPTIONS: A the-stoa forge-owned at substrate/skills/builder-deploy/ (couples to the substrate-deploy lifecycle; non-the-stoa consumers carry substrate weight) ~ B standalone builder-tooling home (decoupled cadence but stands up a home for a consumer that barely exists yet) ~ A-with-graduation-trigger (A now; graduate to B when either a 2nd non-the-stoa consumer appears OR release cadence must diverge; the move is an additive git mv since the layout is HOME-independent)
CHOSEN: A-with-graduation-trigger (A now; graduate to B when either a 2nd non-the-stoa consumer appears OR release cadence must diverge; the move is an additive git mv since the layout is HOME-independent)
COUNTER-HYPOTHESIS: if at the A-to-B graduation the relocation requires more than an additive git mv plus a consume-path update — i.e. it forces a redesign of the builder_deploy_core package layout or its data/ plus tests/ structure — then the HOME-independent-layout premise was false and A-with-trigger was the wrong call; equally, if a 2nd non-the-stoa consumer appears and is forced to install the entire the-stoa substrate just to obtain builder-deploy before graduation completes, the discoverability-over-coupling bet landed wrong.
CONTEXT-LINK: stoa--k48 (u--9s2 Phase-2 inc 2.3); ratified by Polybius_the_Stoa 2026-06-27T04:34:57Z; supersedes the 2.1 defer entry 2026-06-26T21-32-33Z-home-defer-inc2.1; proposal in chiron-ownership-tier-design.md section 4
